page: Amazon Web Services g5.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for graphics-intensive applications and machine learning inference. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor providing 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores with multithreading) running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. System memory is sized at 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key component of this instance is the single NVIDIA A10G Tensor Core GPU equipped with 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. Storage includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, supplemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark results highlight strong specialized compute while demonstrating clear architectural trade-offs. The single NVIDIA A10G GPU delivers top-tier performance for smaller and medium-sized language models, sustaining prompt processing speeds of 9,378.63 tokens/sec on 135M models and 2,887.79 tokens/sec on 7B models, with corresponding text generation reaching 426.91 tokens/sec and 94.6 tokens/sec respectively. However, 70B parameter models show weak text generation throughput at 2.72 tokens/sec due to the 22 GB VRAM limit. On the CPU side, PassMark testing yields strong results for overall CPU score (55,615.41), encryption tests (68,193.38), and extended instructions (56,952.48). Conversely, single-core stress-ng tests place the CPU in the lower 10th percentile (766.79), confirming that performance gains are concentrated in parallelized and vector workloads rather than single-threaded tasks.

Qualitatively, the g5.16xlarge offers balanced resource density by packaging dedicated CPU cores, substantial host memory, fast local NVMe storage, and an enterprise GPU into a single virtual machine. This configuration eliminates external storage latencies and optimizes operational expenditure for workloads that do not demand multi-GPU clusters. It is directly suited for small-to-medium LLM inference, ray tracing rendering pipelines, video transcode tasks, graphics-heavy virtual workstations, and combined compute-storage pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance designed for GPU-centric workloads and parallel processing. It features 64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor, 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory, a 1900 GB local NVMe SSD, and 25 Gbps network bandwidth. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA A10G GPU with 22 GB of VRAM. Benchmark data exhibits top-tier performance for small-to-medium large language model inference (94.6 tokens/sec generation on 7B models) and strong ray tracing rendering, alongside solid multi-core PassMark CPU and encryption metrics. However, single-core CPU throughput remains low, and large 70B parameter models encounter throughput limitations due to VRAM constraints. This configuration offers high resource density for workloads combining medium-scale machine learning inference, graphics rendering, and local NVMe storage access.
